walkthroughs.body_html:
Textiles — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Textiles brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Textiles.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?

Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares

mcqs.q: What is the rule of thirds?
options: A strict mathematical rule that must never be broken.
A guideline placing key elements along lines or intersections of a 3x3 grid.
Patrons painted the works themselves.
Using exactly three colours.

mcqs.q: Why is understanding patronage important for studying historical art?
options: Using exactly three colours.
Patrons painted the works themselves.
Patrons commissioned art for specific purposes, shaping content and form.
Artists worked freely - patronage was irrelevant to the artwork.

mcqs.q: What did Renaissance artists rediscover that medieval art lacked?
options: Linear perspective and naturalistic representation of the human body.
The use of colour.
Using exactly three colours.
Painting on canvas.
